target_customer: Data scientists and teams deploying Streamlit, Panel, Shiny, Flask and FastAPI apps
problem: Deploying AI and data apps on typical PaaS providers runs into limits on compute and installable libraries.
business_model: Usage based cloud hosting with free community plan and paid tiers
product_category: AI and data app hosting platform (developer tools)

founders.name: Eduardo Blancas
founders.background_notes: From Mexico; author of the open source Ploomber library introduced at JupyterCon 2020 per a PyData speaker profile. Source: YC page.

founders.name: Ido Michael
prior_employers: AWS (led data engineering and data science teams)

exit.reason: A blog post titled that the app hosting platform is shutting down, with deploys ending after October 3, 2025 and final shutdown October 31, 2025; reason not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Container build and deploy pipeline on AWS with scale to zero; standard cloud engineering with some hard operational parts.

defensibility.rationale: Hosting containers is a commodity and free tiers from larger platforms and many Heroku alternatives were available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not confirmed by sources; the company retired its app hosting platform in October 2025.

market_need_then: Open source Ploomber had a user base among data scientists since 2020, and Show HN launch in June 2022 drew interest in running notebooks and apps without infrastructure work.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer friendly, tagline Heroku for AI

branding.community_and_virality: Open source library with GitHub presence and a Product Hunt launch for Ploomber Cloud.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among Python data users through the open source project, but the name is a misspelling that is hard to search and spell.

pivots.from: Notebook and pipeline execution in the cloud (Show HN, June 2022)
pivots.to: Heroku for AI app hosting platform
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; inferred from changed taglines between the Show HN post and the YC page.

outcome_analysis: Ploomber grew out of an open source library and sold hosting for AI and data apps. It reportedly raised only a pre-seed of about 500000 dollars per one aggregator and retired its app hosting platform with final shutdown on October 31, 2025. The cause is not public; the factors listed reflect a commodity hosting market with free offerings from larger platforms and are an inference.
notes: ploomber.io could not be fetched (host not allowed in the session network), so the shutdown rests on the Plushcap listing of the company blog post, whose body did not name the company. Funding rests on one aggregator (Employbl citing Diffbot) and total raised may be incomplete. Pivot date unknown. Competition list left empty: the Show HN mirrors and Porter YC page found were undated or mirrors.
